sources.cite: AWS Security Blog, How to automate incident response in the AWS Cloud for EC2 instances
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. The described order: capture the instance metadata to an S3 bucket before making changes; capture the console view; start snapshots of all EBS volumes; 'Set the Amazon EC2 termination protection flag on the instance'; detach the instance profile; if Systems Manager manages the instance, run OS-level gathering 'such as memory captures'; then 'Create a quarantine security group that lacks both ingress and egress rules' and move the instance into it; notify. The post does not cover Auto Scaling. The EC2 Auto Scaling user guide page 'Use instance scale-in protection to control instance termination' (read 2026-11-18) says EC2 termination protection 'does not prevent Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling from terminating instances'; the DetachInstances API reference (read 2026-11-18) says detached instances can be managed 'independent of the Auto Scaling group', are deregistered from attached target groups, and are not replaced when the desired capacity is decremented.

brief.situation: You are the security engineer on call at Corran Travel. GuardDuty reports one web instance in the booking Auto Scaling group talking to a known cryptocurrency mining pool. The group's scheduled action scales in from 6 to 3 instances at 22:00, and scale-in removes the oldest instances first: this one is the oldest. Legal wants evidence kept for the insurer.
handover: The instance has a root volume and a data volume; its logs are only on the instance (no log shipping for this tier yet).
The instance is managed by Systems Manager.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the compromised instance, its Auto Scaling group, its volumes and logs, and the evidence bucket.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The scheduled scale-in runs at 22:00, 45 minutes after the finding, and would terminate the instance with its local logs and memory.

parts.label: Preserved
parts.modelAnswer: i-0a7e was the oldest instance and scale-in at 22:00 terminates the oldest; its access logs existed only on its disk. Detach from the group and termination protection first, then memory, logs and snapshots to the object-locked evidence bucket with hashes.

parts.label: Contained
parts.modelAnswer: After capture the instance moved to a security group with no rules. Terminating would have destroyed the evidence; a reboot wiped memory and the miner came back from cron.

parts.label: Changes
parts.modelAnswer: The web tier now ships logs to CloudWatch Logs, and the runbook puts detaching and capture before containment.

expertPath.text: Miner on i-0a7e since 19:02; oldest instance, scale-in at 22:00; miner from /tmp as www-data; logs only on disk.
Detach, termination protection, memory and logs, snapshots, quarantine; log shipping and runbook.

evidenceGone.headline: Preserve, then contain
evidenceGone.body: Capture memory, logs and snapshots and protect the instance from termination first; isolate it with a quarantine group, not by deleting it.

scaledIn.headline: Auto Scaling does not wait for forensics
scaledIn.body: Take a compromised instance out of the group (detach it) before the next scaling event; EC2 termination protection alone does not stop Auto Scaling.

preserved.headline: Good: preserve first, then isolate
preserved.body: You read the finding and the scale-in schedule, saw the logs existed only on the instance, detached it from the group, captured memory, logs and volumes, quarantined it, and fixed log shipping.

scoring.modelReasoning: GuardDuty points at one instance, which is the oldest in a group that scales in at 22:00, and the logs that show the entry point exist only on its disk. Detach it from the group and turn on termination protection, capture memory and logs to the evidence bucket, snapshot the volumes, then quarantine it with an empty security group. Terminating destroys the evidence; a reboot wipes memory and the miner returns. Then ship the tier's logs and put preservation first in the runbook.
